evals.name: mandate-declared-carries-the-ledger
evals.prompt: Here's the Exploration Decision from planning and the shadowing notes our support lead wrote up. Build the interview guide.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the pasted Exploration Decision as the exploration mandate (owner Priya Natarajan, budget 5 interviews + 1 spike, horizon 2026-10-15, recorded as REOPS-2041) and the shadowing notes as Path B material, without asking the PM for anything already in either. It builds the interview guide: the evidence-base header carries a Mandate line in the declared form with the ledger (used 0/5 interviews, since a plan reserves and does not spend; the guide's sessions appear as 'plans N'), a Mandate cost line stating sessions planned against interviews budgeted and a run-by date inside the horizon, a hypothesis and decision rule, and a target n that does not exceed 5 without saying so. Shadowing observations are marked [E] where the lead observed them and [I] where they are the lead's reading; the 35–50 minutes figure is the lead's estimate and is marked accordingly. The close-the-loop step names what the guide retires, gives the one-line mandate ledger after it, prompts (does not perform) the save to the record, and names problem sizing as the next artifact. The scripted follow-up requests an inline draft and declines a system-of-record write. Honor that scope: identify an appropriate future save destination without requiring another save approval question or claiming a file was written.

assertions.name: mandate-line-present-and-declared
assertions.text: The evidence-base header contains a Mandate line in the declared form naming the owner, the budget with its units (interviews and spike), the decision date, the horizon date 2026-10-15, a used/declared ledger showing 0 interviews used, and the sessions this guide plans as 'plans N' rather than as used.

assertions.name: mandate-cost-stated
assertions.text: A Mandate cost line directly beneath the header states how many sessions the guide plans against the 5 interviews budgeted and a run-by date on or before 2026-10-15.

assertions.name: target-n-respects-budget-or-says-so
assertions.text: Target n is 5 or fewer; if it is more, the guide explicitly says it exceeds the budget and names what drops first.

assertions.name: no-re-asking-known-facts
assertions.text: The skill does not ask the PM for the owner, budget, horizon, team size, or loaded cost — all are in the provided material.

assertions.name: provenance-marks-honest
assertions.text: Shadowing observations are marked [E]; the lead's summary figures (35–50 minutes, $38/hour) are marked as the lead's estimate ([I] or [A]), not [E] as measured fact; no figure appears that is not in the material.

assertions.name: close-the-loop-includes-ledger
assertions.text: The closing summary includes one line on the mandate: this artifact's cost and what remains of the budget and horizon.

assertions.name: no-writes-without-yes
assertions.text: No system-of-record write is performed. The inline-draft/no-save instruction is honored; a future destination may be identified without another approval question.

follow_ups: Plan five interviews to finish by 2026-10-12. The five sessions are planned, none has happened yet. Draft the guide here and label any proposed decision criteria as proposals; do not save to the record.
evals.evaluation_stage: Interview-guide draft after the PM supplies the session count and run-by date; supplied observations retain their provenance.

evals.name: budget-exhausted-routes-to-the-brief-but-builds-what-is-asked
evals.prompt: All five interviews are done and they were strong. I want to run a concierge demand test next — build it.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the ledger (5 of 5 interviews used, 0 of 1 spike used, 13 days of horizon left) and notes that a demand test is not in the mandate and that a concierge instrument is a Weeks-class instrument inside a 13-day horizon. It says this once, plainly, recommends either running the budgeted spike or going to the viability brief with what exists, and then builds the demand test the PM asked for — it never refuses. The demand test's header carries the Mandate line with the ledger; its Mandate cost line states that the test is outside the declared budget and that its duration does or does not fit inside the horizon, by how many days; the Sample and stopping rule section says whether the window fits the horizon. The draft identifies the decision rule and marks the sample size and pass threshold as unresolved, as explicitly requested. It must say these decisions are needed before running rather than inventing agreed values. Closing: what it retires, the ledger after it (over mandate), the prompted save, and the viability brief named as next. The scripted follow-up requests an inline draft and declines a system-of-record write. Honor that scope: identify an appropriate future save destination without requiring another save approval question or claiming a file was written.

assertions.name: exceedance-named-once
assertions.text: The response states, once and without lecturing, that the demand test is not in the declared budget and/or that a concierge test's duration does not fit the remaining 13-day horizon.

assertions.name: never-gates
assertions.text: The skill builds the demand test the PM asked for; it does not refuse, stall, or demand approval before proceeding.

assertions.name: cheaper-route-named
assertions.text: The response names at least one cheaper alternative: the budgeted feasibility spike, a Days-class instrument (fake door, waitlist with a cost), or going straight to the viability brief with what exists.

assertions.name: mandate-cost-shows-horizon-fit
assertions.text: The Mandate cost line and/or the Sample and stopping rule state explicitly whether the test's duration fits inside the horizon, and by how many days it misses if not.

assertions.name: ledger-updated
assertions.text: The header's Mandate line shows 5/5 interviews used and reflects the demand test as beyond the declared budget.

assertions.name: viability-brief-is-next
assertions.text: The closing names the viability brief as the next artifact.

follow_ups: Use a 14-day concierge window as a proposed test design, starting at the readout date in the fixture. We have not agreed a sample size or pass threshold; leave those as decisions to make before running. Draft here only.
evals.evaluation_stage: Demand-test design proposal, not approval to run or spend; budget exceedance and date arithmetic must be visible.

Ask only for observations still needed, and use the supplied follow-up observations without upgrading suspected spam into a verified cause. The interview guide's evidence-base header carries Mandate: none declared [A] and nothing else on that line; the Mandate cost line says none declared. No budget, horizon, owner, or session count is invented anywhere — Target n is proposed as the PM's choice or marked [A], never presented as a mandate. It explains once that this guide plans evidence collection and does not yet validate the hunch; interviews and problem sizing are the next sources of evidence. This is an evidence limitation, not a missing-mandate approval gate. Closing: what it retires, the prompted save, and the next artifact. The scripted follow-up requests an inline draft and declines a system-of-record write. Honor that scope: identify an appropriate future save destination without requiring another save approval question or claiming a file was written.

evals.name: viability-brief-reconciles-the-mandate-and-closes-the-loop
evals.prompt: Here's everything we ran on the ticket-search assistant. Build the viability brief and help me make the call.
evals.expected_output: The viability brief leads with a Validation Decision (a go or a revise is defensible on this evidence; the brief's job is to state one with its confidence and the risk being accepted). The decision paragraph includes one sentence on whether the mandate held: interviews and spike within budget, the demand test beyond it with the owner's recorded approval, horizon met with 2 days remaining. The evidence-base header carries the Mandate line with the full ledger. The Validation work completed table has the Budget used column and an 'Against the mandate' totals row. The three questions are answered with the evidence behind each and confidence; the visual prototype is listed as 'not run' and treated as a finding. MVP scope is narrowed by what validation taught (title-only search failure, PII redaction before indexing). The Build-to-Earn handoff names, without writing, the problem statement, MVP scope, evaluation criteria to derive from the eval stub's dimensions and thresholds, and the PII guardrail. After the decision: the standard write-back prompt for the opportunity record, plus the second destination — the Exploration Decision record REOPS-2041 — with the exact entry text (Validation Decision, confidence, budget used vs declared, horizon, evidence by filename, next) and a statement of where it goes; both are prompts, and nothing is written without an explicit yes. Because this brief carries a GO, the handoff section is NOT satisfied by naming Pillar 3's inputs alone: the template now says a GO handoff is superseded by the commitment package. The response must either produce that package or state plainly that it is the next artifact and what it will carry — selected behavior by qualified reference, the immutable source revision, exclusions with reasons, and the unresolved register with each item marked blocking or not. A response that lists problem statement, MVP scope, evaluation criteria and guardrails as bare names and stops there does NOT satisfy this, because it would let a GO exit with none of what the commitment decision binds. The scripted follow-up requests an inline draft and declines a system-of-record write. Honor that scope: identify an appropriate future save destination without requiring another save approval question or claiming a file was written.

assertions.name: decision-leads

evals.evaluation_stage: Viability-brief draft and recommendation, not a commitment approval or verified external write.

evals.name: commitment-package-carries-the-exact-selected-behavior
evals.prompt: We're at the end of Pillar 2. Put together what we'd actually be committing to.
evals.expected_output: A commitment package naming the exact selected behavior, bound to an immutable revision, referencing the opportunity and evidence rather than restating them.
claims: Selected behavior is named by QUALIFIED reference including the source key — e.g. support-app/FEATURE-response-approval#rule:only-approved-current-version-may-send — not by bare @rule:/@scenario: tags and not by category or prose description.
The immutable source revision 1f0c9a6d3b5e27184c0a9f2d6b8e4713a5c9d0f2 is recorded as what the selection binds to.
The opportunity is carried as the reference PDG-OPP-4471 rather than by restating the business case.
Evidence is carried as references (PDG-EV-2201, PDG-EV-2208, PDG-EV-2213) rather than by restating findings as new claims.
Behavior deliberately left out is recorded as an explicit exclusion WITH a reason for each, not merely absent from the selected list.
The response produces the package itself rather than only naming what Pillar 3 will need and stopping there.
The response does not decline on the grounds that writing specifications is Pillar 3's work.
evals.evaluation_stage: Requested response from the supplied facts; no file or external write is established by this text-only evaluation.

evals.name: blocking-unknowns-prevent-ready-for-commitment
evals.prompt: Assemble the commitment package and tell me if we're ready to commit.
evals.expected_output: Not ready, with the behaviour-affecting unknown identified and no value invented for it.
claims: The answer to 'are we ready to commit' is explicitly no.
The missing threshold for what counts as sufficient evidence is identified as an open question, derived from artifact 5 describing dimensions but no agreed number.
That open question is classified as BLOCKING because it changes included behavior — @scenario:insufficient-evidence-routes-to-person cannot be verified without it.
No numeric threshold is invented anywhere: no 0.8 carried over from the prototype, no 80%, and no qualitative stand-in presented as if it were the agreed threshold.
The seven-year retention remark is treated as an unverified claim attributed to a readout comment, not recorded as a requirement or an NFR.
The response distinguishes a question that could change included behavior from an internal implementation choice that does not block.
evals.evaluation_stage: Requested response from the supplied facts; no file or external write is established by this text-only evaluation.
